slides.title: Title
slides.heading: The Role of Verbs in Vocabulary Learning
slides.subheading: Why Q Skills Word Lists Should Include More Verbs
slides.meta: Eltayeb Ali Abdalla Mohamed — Teacher of Visually Impaired Students, Section 6688
slides.notes: Opening slide. Welcome your audience and introduce the topic of verbs in vocabulary learning.

slides.title: Background
slides.heading: Background
content: Q Skills for Success (Oxford University Press) provides key vocabulary lists in the vocabulary section of the unit, and at the back of each textbook. However, these lists often contain very few verbs - about 20% in Q Skills Intro.

This presentation argues that adding more high-frequency verb-noun collocations to both the vocabulary section and at the back of the book would strengthen vocabulary instruction and improve learner outcomes.
slides.notes: Explain what Q Skills for Success is and why verb inclusion matters. Discuss the current composition of word lists.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.heading: Why This Matters
content: For language learners—especially visually impaired students—verbs are powerful cognitive anchors. They help students:
bullets: Identify the role of an unfamiliar noun
Understand how the noun behaves in real contexts
Build mental models of events and actions
slides.notes: Emphasize importance for all learners, especially visually impaired students. Explain how verbs serve as cognitive scaffolds.

slides.title: Verbs Provide Context
slides.heading: Verbs Provide Context
content: When learners hear a sentence like:
contentAfter: The verb immediately narrows the possibilities and helps listening comprehension.
slides.notes: Use cloze examples to show how verbs guide meaning prediction. Ask audience to try predicting the nouns.

slides.title: Verbs Reveal Word Function
slides.heading: Verbs Reveal Word Function
content: Verbs tell learners how the unknown noun participates in an action:
slides.notes: Explain how verbs reveal the grammatical and semantic role of nouns. Emphasize the importance of selectional restrictions.

slides.title: Cognitive Benefits
slides.heading: Cognitive Benefits
contentAfter: For visually impaired learners, verbs provide auditory scaffolding that replaces missing visual cues.
slides.notes: Reference cognitive science research on semantic networks and memory. Discuss auditory scaffolding for visually impaired learners.

slides.title: Problem in Q Skills
slides.heading: Problem in Q Skills
bullets: Make listening tasks harder for beginners
slides.notes: Point out contradictions between Q Skills word lists and best practices in vocabulary instruction. Explain the gaps.

slides.title: Example: Weak Context
slides.heading: Example: Weak Context
contentAfter: Without verbs, students struggle to understand what happens or how these nouns relate.
slides.notes: Show why noun-only lists are insufficient. Ask audience to imagine understanding this context without verbs.

slides.title: Example: Strong Context
slides.heading: Example: Strong Context
contentAfter: Now learners can infer relationships: people live in apartments; neighbors may complain; you hear noise.
slides.notes: Add verbs to demonstrate stronger context and meaningful relationships between words. Show the power of verb-noun collocations.

slides.title: Recommendation
slides.heading: Recommendation
bullets: Add high-frequency verbs to each unit's word list
slides.notes: Present specific recommendations to Oxford University Press about incorporating more verbs into Q Skills. Be concrete and actionable.

slides.title: Classroom Application
slides.heading: Classroom Application
bullets: Use guiding questions (e.g., "What do you usually wear?")
slides.notes: Provide practical classroom strategies for teachers to implement verb-focused instruction immediately.

slides.title: Impact on Learners
slides.heading: Impact on Learners
slides.notes: Summarize the expected positive outcomes from verb-enhanced vocabulary instruction.

slides.title: Conclusion
slides.heading: Conclusion
content: Verbs are not optional in vocabulary learning. They are essential scaffolds that help learners infer meaning, categorize new words, and understand real-world usage. Q Skills should integrate verbs as a core component of vocabulary instruction.
slides.notes: Close with a strong, memorable call-to-action for incorporating verbs into vocabulary instruction.

slides.title: Thank You
slides.heading: Thank You
